bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the manuscript's title page
bibliography.note: Authors and title match. The NOAA copy is the accepted manuscript (48 pages, line-numbered); the version of record is CJFAS 82: 1–15. Page numbers below are the manuscript's.

claims.claim: in the Weldon Dam reservoir on the Penobscot in spring 2022, 390 tethered Atlantic salmon smolts were deployed and chain pickerel (43 events) and smallmouth bass (42) were the only predators
claims.source_value: 390 tethered smolts over 16 days, April 23–May 24 (2022); 85 (21.8 %) were eaten, 43 by chain pickerel (11.0 %) and 42 by smallmouth bass (10.8 %)
claims.location: p. 14 (PDF p. 14), Results, lines 312–315; abstract p. 2, lines 29–31
claims.quote: and predators consisted of chain pickerel (n=43, 11.0%
claims.conditions: smolts tethered to drifting camera rigs, deployments limited to about one hour; Weldon Dam reservoir, Penobscot River, Maine
claims.note: The counts are smolts eaten, i.e. predation events. The authors call both predators 'not native to the study area' (abstract).

claims.claim: 23 % of tethered smolts were taken within an hour
claims.source_value: the best hazard model estimated 22.7 % (95 % CI 15.4–29.5 %) would be taken within a 60-min deployment; observed, 21.8 % (85 of 390) were taken during deployments that averaged about an hour
claims.quote: The most supported hazard model estimated that on average, 22.7%
claims.note: This is a model estimate; 'an estimated 23 %' would be exact.

claims.claim: the probability of predation within a one-hour deployment rose from about 10 % at 5 °C to 33 % at 15 °C
claims.quote: and predation probability increased from 10% to 33% when temperature
claims.conditions: the model's prediction for a one-hour deployment; water temperature HR = 1.93 (95 % CI 1.43–2.60)

claims.claim: smolts within 40 m of shore were at above-average risk
claims.source_value: above-average risk within 40 m of shore; the model predicted > 24 % predated within 40 m. Risk fell with distance from shore (HR = 0.56)
claims.location: abstract p. 2 (PDF p. 2), lines 35–36; p. 21 (PDF p. 21), lines 467–469; p. 15, lines 328–329
claims.quote: Smolts also incurred above-average predation risk within 40 m
claims.conditions: distance to an NHD shoreline widened by 12 m
claims.note: The authors add that nearness to shore mattered less in warmer water (an interaction whose CI included 1).

notes: All claims check against the full manuscript, so the paper's 'abstract only' labels (§3.5.7, §3.7.1) can be dropped. Other useful values: average time to predation 24.9 min (range 0.4–59.9 min); larger smolts were at lower risk (fork length HR = 0.77); predation hotspots were in structured, shallow backwaters and constrictions (7 of 18 smolts eaten off one island's narrow channel); the reservoir is mostly shallow (< 2 m) sediment flats with sparse macrophytes and submerged stumps. For §2.5: the authors treat chain pickerel and smallmouth as non-native in the Penobscot study area.
